headline: INDIA DOESN'T JUST NEED MORE SOLAR CAPACITY. IT NEEDS MORE USABLE SOLAR ENERGY
INDIA DOESN'T JUST NEED MORE SOLAR CAPACITY. IT NEEDS MORE USABLE SOLAR ENERGY
caption:
INDIA DOESN'T JUST NEED MORE SOLAR CAPACITY. IT NEEDS MORE USABLE SOLAR ENERGY.

We're great at adding megawatts. But a megawatt that can't reach a consumer when they need it is a stranded asset.

Our solar peaks around noon. Our grid stress peaks after sunset, when the sun is gone and demand is highest.

That mismatch is the real bottleneck. Every evening, coal and gas still fill the gap that solar can't.

The fix isn't only more panels. A few hours of battery storage paired with solar can shift midday generation into the evening peak, which turns cheap daytime power into firm, dispatchable supply.

Tenders that reward firm, time-matched power over raw capacity would change what gets built.

Are we measuring solar success by what we install, or by what we actually deliver when India needs it?

#IndiaEnergy #SolarEnergy #EnergyStorage

headline: everyone is talking about solar
caption:
Everyone is talking about solar. Few are talking about 4 PM.

India added record solar capacity last year, yet in states like Rajasthan, midday generation is already being curtailed because the grid can't absorb it. Meanwhile, demand peaks after sunset, when we fall back on coal and expensive gas.

The problem isn't generating cheap power. It's generating it when and where we can use it.

Solar at ₹2.5/unit looks great. But add storage, transmission losses, and balancing costs, and the real price of a reliable evening unit looks very different.

That's why the next wave of winners won't be panel installers alone. It'll be those solving for:

• Co-located battery storage
• Green energy corridors that actually get built on time
• Time-of-day tariffs that shift industrial and agricultural load into daylight hours

Capacity is a headline. Dispatchable, usable power is the real milestone.

What's the biggest bottleneck to making solar usable in your state: storage, transmission, or demand?

#SolarEnergy #EnergyTransition #India

Cheap generation is only useful when it meets demand.

Transmission, storage, and smarter demand all need to move together with capacity additions.

What do you think will unlock more value for India in the next 3 years: storage, transmission, or demand flexibility?

headline: INDIA'S SOLAR PPA MARKET JUST HIT A NUMBER MOST PEOPLE MISSED: ₹2.87/UNIT.
caption:
INDIA'S SOLAR PPA MARKET JUST HIT A NUMBER MOST PEOPLE MISSED: ₹2.87/UNIT

Cheap, yes. But a unit at noon is not the same product as a unit at 8 pm.

Solar floods the grid when demand is flat and fades when the evening peak arrives. A discom signing a ₹2.87 PPA may still buy expensive power after sunset, and may curtail solar at midday when supply outruns demand.

So the real cost is not the tariff alone. It is the tariff plus what it takes to make those units usable:

→ Storage to shift midday output into the evening
→ Transmission to move power to where demand is
→ Demand matching, such as agricultural feeders and industrial loads shifted to daylight hours

The next phase of India's solar story won't be won by who bids lowest. It will be won by who delivers power when the grid needs it.

Are we pricing solar by the unit, or by the hour it's actually worth?

#SolarEnergy #IndiaEnergy #EnergyTransition

headline: KEARNEY: INDIA'S TRANSMISSION BUILD-OUT MISSED TARGETS BY UP TO 50% WHILE 8 TWH OF SOLAR WENT UNUSED
caption:
Kearney: India's transmission build-out missed targets by up to 50% while 8 TWh of solar went unused

India has built the panels. The wires haven't kept up.

**What the numbers say**

▪ Kearney says more than 8 TWh of solar was curtailed in Q1 FY2027. That is close to 2% of all electricity generated in the quarter and roughly a fifth of solar output.

▪ The Renewable Energy Minister's figures are consistent: 2,417 GWh in April, 3,235 GWh in May and 2,481 GWh in June. The government cited a mismatch between transmission and renewable project commissioning. The total is 8,133 GWh.

▪ Kearney's analysis of CEA data shows annual transmission additions have consistently missed National Electricity Plan targets, with shortfalls as high as 50% in some years.

**Why it matters**

ICRA found about 33% of 54.8 GW of recently commissioned renewable capacity was being evacuated through temporary GNA as of May 2026. Curtailment under T-GNA is highest during solar hours, at 50–60%.

The catch-up bill is large. The ISTS rolling plan calls for 67,263 circuit km of lines and 629,597 MVA of transformation capacity by FY2030–31, at an estimated INR 4.85 lakh crore.

**The solar-park implication**

A solar park is only as valuable as its ability to evacuate power. Commissioning ahead of the grid means paying for generation that may never be sold.

Grid access has to be treated as a core bankability factor, alongside land, modules and the PPA.

**Kearney's practical levers**

Kearney says co-locating storage can free up to 60% of tied-up grid capacity. FACTS and dynamic line rating can add 20–30% more throughput on existing lines.

**The key insight**

Kearney's view is that India has an execution and utilization gap, not a funding gap. Building more lines matters, and so does using the existing ones better.

For us at DeCircle Solar, this is a reminder that solar-park planning starts with evacuation, not with panel count.

**Question for the industry:** Should connectivity and storage be planned together with every new solar park from day one, rather than added after curtailment starts?

#SolarEnergy #India #Transmission #Curtailment #SolarPark #GridInfrastructure #EnergyStorage #RenewableEnergy

headline: RAJASTHAN TENDERS 900 MW / 5,400 MWH RAMPURA PUMPED STORAGE AS SOLAR CURTAILMENT PERSISTS
caption:
Rajasthan tenders 900 MW / 5,400 MWh Rampura pumped storage as solar curtailment persists

Rajasthan is putting long-duration storage next to its solar belt.

**What happened**

Rajasthan Renewable Energy Corporation (RRECL) has invited global bids for the 900 MW/5,400 MWh Rampura Pumped Storage Project in Tonk. It will be built on a Build-Own-Operate-Transfer basis through tariff-based competitive bidding, followed by an e-reverse auction.

**Key numbers**

▪ Bid security: ₹108 crore
▪ Pre-bid meeting: 27 October 2026
▪ Bids due: 30 November 2026
▪ 5,400 MWh at 900 MW works out to about six hours of full-power discharge

**Why it matters**

The tender follows a grid problem that new transmission has not fixed. At a December 2025 stakeholder meeting, roughly 4 GW remained restricted during the peak solar window between 11 am and 2 pm. This was even after the Khetri–Narela line was commissioned.

Officials cited voltage oscillations at renewable energy complexes, low short-circuit ratios at pooling stations, and overloaded lines.

**Solar-park implication**

Solar parks produce the most at midday, which is when evacuation is tightest. Storage that can absorb midday output and release it later could cut curtailment and protect project revenue.

A tender is not a plant, though. Pumped storage takes years to build, so developers will keep facing curtailment risk in the meantime.

**Key insight**

For large solar parks, the constraint is shifting from module cost to evacuation capacity and the ability to move energy across the day.

At DeCircle Solar, we track how grid limits and storage shape solar-park economics.

**Question:** Will long-duration storage like pumped hydro ease curtailment faster than new transmission, or do both need to arrive together?

#SolarEnergy #PumpedStorage #EnergyStorage #Rajasthan #Curtailment #SolarParks #RenewableEnergy #IndiaEnergy

headline: CRISIL: INDIA'S BESS BOOM FACES A PRICE SQUEEZE, WITH 12 GWH OF BATTERY PROJECTS AT RISK
caption:
India's BESS boom faces a price squeeze: Crisil flags 12 GWh of battery projects at risk

India's storage pipeline is growing fast. The economics behind part of it are getting harder.

**What Crisil said**

India could commission 45–50 GWh of BESS capacity over FY2027 and FY2028, compared with about 1 GWh by the end of FY2026. Around 50–55 GWh is currently scheduled for commissioning in those two fiscals. Distribution utilities are expected to account for around 40 GWh of it.

**Where the pressure is**

Nearly 21% of under-construction BESS capacity, about 12 GWh, faces weak return potential.

The cause is price timing. Crisil says battery prices fell from $118/kWh in 2024 to $50–55/kWh in 2025, then rebounded to $70–75/kWh in 2026. Many tariffs were bid when prices were lower. Developers generally procure batteries around a year after securing project bids.

At prevailing battery prices, returns may fall short of the typical 12–14% target IRR. Developers may defer implementation in anticipation of more favourable battery pricing.

Of the 12 GWh, around 8–9 GWh also faces execution risk because sponsors have limited implementation experience.

**Why it matters for solar parks**

Many solar-park developers count on co-located storage to reduce curtailment and move output into evening hours. If storage-linked projects slip, commissioning dates and revenue assumptions could slip with them.

This is my own reading of the Crisil data, not a Crisil finding.

**The key insight**

A storage tariff bets on procurement timing as much as on technology. Bids that assumed batteries would keep getting cheaper now carry the risk of that assumption failing.

At DeCircle Solar, we treat storage timelines as a risk to model, not an assumption to lock in.

**Your view**

Should storage-linked solar parks be built in phases, with solar commissioned first and BESS added later, to protect timelines?

#BESS #EnergyStorage #SolarParks #IndiaEnergy #RenewableEnergy #Crisil #BatteryStorage #DeCircleSolar

headline: THE ACRE THAT DOES TWO JOBS AT ONCE Solar and farming
caption:
THE ACRE THAT DOES TWO JOBS AT ONCE: Solar and farming

Land is the quiet bottleneck of utility-scale solar. Every project competes with food production, grazing and local priorities.

Agrivoltaics answers this directly. Panels mounted on a structure generate electricity while crops grow underneath.

**What the evidence shows**

📍 Fraunhofer ISE's pilot near Lake Constance, Germany, showed a land use efficiency of 160% in 2017. Based on 2018 potato yields, it rose to 186%.

📍 A recent review found land equivalent ratios typically between 1.2 and 1.6 across most system types.

📍 A 2026 global modelling study found agrivoltaics need 30× less land than bioenergy for the same electricity output.

**The catch**

Results depend on the crop and the design. Shade-tolerant vegetables and orchards performed well, while cereals were less productive.

Cost matters too. One small-scale farmer study put agrivoltaic electricity at 9.40 cents/kWh against 8.40 for PV-only, which is 11.9% higher. Crop revenue and avoided land acquisition costs can offset that.

**Why it matters for solar parks**

Dual use can ease land-use conflicts and make projects easier to defend locally. It also changes engineering decisions. Mounting height, row spacing and crop choice all have to be settled at design stage, not retrofitted later.

**Key insight**

The strongest agrivoltaic projects start with what the farmer needs, then design the array around it.

At DeCircle Solar, we see smart land use as part of building solar parks that last.

**Question:** What is the biggest barrier to co-designing solar parks with farmers from day one: economics, regulation or trust?

#Agrivoltaics #SolarEnergy #SolarParks #RenewableEnergy #Agriculture #LandUse #CleanEnergy #DeCircleSolar

headline: INDIA'S RECORD 27 GW SOLAR HALF-YEAR HIDES A SLUMP IN UTILITY-SCALE BUILD AND AUCTIONS
caption:
**India's record 27 GW solar half-year hides a slump in utility-scale build and auctions**

India added a record 27 GW of solar in H1 2026, up 49% from 18 GW a year earlier. Cumulative capacity reached about 165 GW by June, according to Mercom India Research.

The second quarter tells a different story.

**📉 What the numbers show**

• Q2 additions were about 12 GW, down 24% from 15 GW in Q1.
• Utility-scale solar was about 8 GW in Q2, down 37% quarter on quarter and 23% year on year.
• Tenders were about 5 GW, down 22% year on year.
• Auctions were about 2 GW, down 40% year on year and 56% quarter on quarter.

**⚙️ Why the slowdown**

Mercom blames limited supply and higher prices of ALMM-compliant domestic cells. Developers also rushed to finish projects before the ALMM List-II and ISTS deadlines, which pulled volume into the first months of the year.

**🔌 The solar-park implication**

Mercom CEO Raj Prabhu said several projects are nearing completion but cannot connect to the grid because evacuation infrastructure isn't ready.

For solar parks, land and modules are no longer the only constraint. Grid readiness and cell supply now decide when a plant earns revenue.

Concentration adds risk. Gujarat, Rajasthan and Maharashtra took 40%, 19% and 17% of Q2 utility-scale additions, so any transmission delay in these states affects the national number.

**💡 Key insight**

A big pipeline is not the same as commissioned capacity. Mercom counts 208 GW of large-scale projects in the pipeline, but says it won't turn into installed capacity at current forecast levels unless the bottlenecks are fixed.

The H1 record looks like a pull-forward before the deadlines, not a sustainable run-rate.

At DeCircle Solar, we watch this closely. Solar park economics depend on grid connection and cell availability as much as on module price.

**❓ Over to you**

Which will limit utility-scale solar more in the next 12 months: transmission readiness or domestic cell supply?

#SolarEnergy #IndiaSolar #SolarPark #UtilityScaleSolar #RenewableEnergy #ALMM #GridInfrastructure #DeCircleSolar

headline: MAHARASHTRA REGULATOR EASES AVAADA'S 2 GW SOLAR DEADLINES AS STATE GRID UPGRADES SLIP INTO FY2028-29
caption:
**MERC eases Avaada's 2 GW solar deadlines as Maharashtra grid upgrades slip into FY2028-29**

The solar projects are ready to be built. The grid that has to carry their power is not.

**What happened**

On 1 October 2026, the Maharashtra Electricity Regulatory Commission (MERC) gave in-principle approval to review the Scheduled Commencement of Supply Dates (SCSDs) for solar projects of Avaada Energy and three subsidiaries.

The developers hold PPAs with MSEDCL for about 2 GW of combined solar and wind power. Their original SCSDs fell between 2025 and 2027.

**The numbers**

▪ MSETCL's transmission strengthening and network augmentation is now expected to finish between FY2027-28 and FY2028-29.
▪ Avaada expects delays of about 5 to 19 months across different solar components.
▪ It is not seeking an extension for its wind assets, because the evacuation constraints affect only the solar projects.

**Why it matters**

Avaada argued that it cannot start scheduled supply without adequate transmission. It also argued that it could face contractual penalties for delays outside its control.

MERC noted that transmission delays beyond a developer's control could fall under the PPAs' Force Majeure provisions. The Commission also directed the petitioners to submit a comprehensive representation.

This is an in-principle approval to review the dates, not a final extension.

**The solar-park angle**

For solar-park developers, this is a clear signal. Modules, land and EPC capacity can all be ready, but a project still cannot earn revenue until power can be evacuated.

Developers with state PPAs should check now whether their SCSDs line up with the transmission provider's realistic timelines. If they don't, they may need to file for relief early to avoid penalties.

**Key insight**

Grid readiness, not module or land availability, is increasingly setting commissioning timelines.

At DeCircle Solar, we follow these regulatory and grid developments because they directly affect how solar parks are planned, phased and financed.

**Question for the industry:** Should transmission milestones be built into PPA timelines from day one, so developers aren't left to seek regulatory relief after the fact?

#SolarEnergy #SolarPark #Maharashtra #MERC #Transmission #RenewableEnergy #IndiaEnergy #DeCircleSolar

headline: SECI LAUNCHES 800 MW / 3,200 MWH STANDALONE BESS TENDER WITH A 30 APRIL 2027 COMMISSIONING DEADLINE
caption:
SECI launches an 800 MW / 3,200 MWh standalone BESS tender, and the commissioning deadline is 30 April 2027.

The RfS was issued on 1 October 2026 as SECI-ESS-IV. It seeks standalone battery storage equal to four hours of discharge, with awards decided by electronic reverse auction.

**What the tender says**

• Projects follow a build-own-operate model, with SECI acting as intermediary procurer.
• The buying entity schedules discharge for any four hours between 17:00 on one day and 11:00 the next.
• Bidders must arrange charging power, with at least 51% of the charging energy from renewable sources.
• The pre-bid meeting is on 7 October, online bids close on 30 October, and technical bids open on 4 November.
• The project deadline is 30 April 2027, about seven months after issue.

**Why it matters**

India curtailed more than 8 TWh of solar between April and June 2026, with grid congestion a major factor. Storage that can be dispatched on demand moves energy from the solar peak into the evening. SECI is still buying exactly that.

**What it means for solar parks**

Solar parks already hold the assets a storage project needs: land, grid connectivity and an existing evacuation route. Developers who can use these should have an edge in the auction.

The deadline is short. A bidder that has not secured connectivity, land and battery supply before 30 October will struggle to commission on time. Meeting the deadline will depend heavily on these three things.

**Key insight**

In this tender, readiness is as important as price. The lowest bid means little if the project cannot connect and commission by April 2027. Bankable, shovel-ready sites will decide who wins.

At DeCircle Solar, we track tenders like this because storage is becoming part of solar-park planning, not an add-on.

**Over to you**

Should new solar parks be planned with storage from day one, or is standalone BESS the better route?

#SolarEnergy #BESS #EnergyStorage #SECI #IndiaRenewables #SolarPark #GridIntegration #CleanEnergy

headline: CERC GIVES RAJASTHAN'S 250 MW KHABA SOLAR PROJECT 45 MORE DAYS TO INJECT INFIRM POWER
caption:
CERC gives Rajasthan's 250 MW Khaba solar project 45 more days to inject infirm power

The last 38.1 MW of a large Barmer project has been given more time to finish commissioning.

**What happened**
CERC granted Khaba Renewable Energy a 45-day extension to inject infirm power from the remaining 38.1 MW. The order was issued on 25 September 2026. It also condoned a six-day delay in filing the petition.

**The numbers**
▪ The petition covered a 221 MW tranche. NRLDC gave it first-time charging approval on 2 March 2026.
▪ The Grid Code allows an initial 45 days. NRLDC then extended this to 15 July 2026.
▪ By August, 200 MW of the 250 MW was commissioned.
▪ The company first said 42 MW remained. It later corrected this to 38.1 MW.

**What caused the delay**
The developer cited repeated theft of modules, string cables and connectors. Other problems were severe weather, right-of-way obstructions and the shifting of an 11 kV line. A storm on 1 June 2026 reportedly damaged about 2,891 modules.

**Why it matters for solar parks**
The project was split into tranches so it could get charging approvals and commission in phases. Each tranche has its own approvals and its own regulatory clock.

When one block runs late, the clock can expire on capacity that is already built. CERC also directed that extensions granted by regional load despatch centres be recorded in writing, with reasons for the delay.

**Key insight**
Commissioning risk is no longer only about modules and EPC schedules. Site security, weather resilience and managing the regulatory clock now matter just as much.

Developers should plan for them from day one.

**Where DeCircle Solar fits**
At DeCircle Solar, we follow how events like this shape the full solar-park lifecycle, from commissioning to end of life.

**Question for you**
Should regulators build a standard extension process for tranche-based solar parks, or should every delay be judged case by case?

#SolarEnergy #Rajasthan #CERC #RenewableEnergy #SolarParks #IndiaSolar #EnergyTransition #DeCircleSolar
